biome_primitives.name: One world: from a point to a passage
biome_primitives.description: Full-size 12 × 12 metre walkable ground, from point/line/trace/grid to triangulated panels and five equal solids with unequal passages. Authored hall stage, walking-driven trace, no in-world interface. Prototype, not installed in the spine. Rotation revisits the thin faces as an automatic bank of hinged panels, holding their angle while the tracked visitor occupies a sweep. Scale repeats the same hinge movement at two widths, changing width only while closed; the grid and walking body keep their dimensions.
interactions: Walk across the ground: your projected position moves.
In the line stage, compare your walk with the straight relation to its reference.
In trace and grid stages, your walking leaves sampled marks; the grid highlights the occupied cell.
Walk around the triangulated panels; compare face-on and edge-on views.
Try the gaps between equal volumes. The standalone 0.5 metre capsule cannot pass the 0.35 metre gap.
Watch the hinged faces turn, then enter a sweep to hold their angle. The left-edge pivots stay fixed.
Compare the same passage before and after the panels widen. The fixed hinge and metre grid make the change measurable.
biome_primitives.qfep_connection: An address and a sampled record preserve selected differences; withdrawal reveals which capabilities depend on a rule. This is an early encounter, not a QFEP implementation.
